hypothesis: A rare wrong half-cycle phase may reveal itself as a stable long-context reorganization in which the half-cycle grid suppresses 2-beat periodicity while materially strengthening 3-beat periodicity across a sufficiently long existing tempo segment. This is a directional cross-periodicity hypothesis, not a retune of selector v1.

rule.candidate: exact half-cycle phase relative to currently selected phase at unchanged BPM
rule.multi_segment_policy: evaluate each existing segment independently; do not alter segment boundaries or BPM
rule.canonical_output_policy: shadow-only until independent validation and implementation regression testing

selector_v1_separation: Selector v1 required median beat-strength gain, any of g2/g3/g4 periodicity gain, and a mean beat-confidence floor.
Selector v2 does not use median beat strength or mean beat confidence.
Selector v2 requires a directional relationship between two distinct long-context periodicities plus minimum repeated-window evidence.
No selector-v1 threshold was moved or reused as a hidden gate.
scientific_guardrails: The failed ASAP/MAESTRO V1 holdout was not used as validation for this rule and must not be described as independent evidence for V2.
Because the ASAP corpus has already been opened for selector-v1 evaluation, any V2 evaluation on it is post-hoc regression screening only.
Do not retune V2 thresholds from the burned ASAP corpus.
If V2 shows a catastrophic regression on any burned-corpus trigger, reject V2 rather than patching tracks or moving thresholds.
Any claim of V2 validation requires a genuinely new frozen independent holdout selected before its Analyzer-derived V2 evidence is inspected.
Do not add track IDs, composers, genres, annotation labels, or benchmark-specific exceptions.
No production phase switch is authorized by this file.
